content.text:
The report is written and validated at `/app/report.json`. Summary of what I found:

**Cause: mixture.** The shipped eval slice has a measured leak of about 0.44, which is why the offline number looked clean. Decontaminated scoring exposed the regression and isolated the knob:

| config (decontaminated offline slice) | score |
|---|---|
| release as shipped | 0.741 to 0.747 |
| only mixture restored to 0.760 | 0.796 to 0.800 |
| only mixture reset to recipe 1.0 | 0.791 |
| only capacity restored to 0.759 | 0.762 |
| only lr_scale restored to 1.198 | 0.736 |
| capacity and lr_scale both reset to recipe, mixture at release | 0.775 |

Restoring mixture alone recovers nearly all of the drop, and resetting the other two knobs while holding mixture at its release value leaves most of the regression in place. That satisfies the counterfactual test in both directions.

**Fix shipped in the report:** mixture 0.760 plus capacity 0.759, both at the maximum the release note permits. Adding capacity on top of mixture lifts the decontaminated score to 0.805 to 0.812, the best reachable under the constraint. Restoring lr_scale to 1.198 on top of that config hurt, and pushing it to 1.4 also hurt, so lr_scale stays at its release value.

Budget used: 15 of 20 re-runs. No canary was needed because the decontaminated offline slice reproduced the online drop and removed the leak confound.
